facts.label: Audited FY2025 results
facts.text: - Revenues were 49,573 USD m, up from 48,611 USD m in FY2024 (an increase of 962). Operating expenses fell from 41,239 USD m to 40,197 USD m. Credit loss expense was 524 USD m against 551 USD m (page:371). - Operating profit before tax rose from 6,821 USD m to 8,853 USD m; the tax expense was 1,056 USD m, giving net profit of 7,797 USD m, of which 7,767 USD m is attributable to shareholders (pages:371 and 372). FY2023 operating profit of 28,255 USD m included negative goodwill of 27,264 USD m from the Credit Suisse acquisition (page:371), so FY2023 is not a run-rate comparative. - The income statement mix is: net interest income 7,747 USD m, other net income from financial instruments at fair value through profit or loss 14,011 USD m, net fee and commission income 27,912 USD m and other income of negative 96 USD m (page:371). Interest income from amortized cost and fair value through other comprehensive income instruments was 27,948 USD m against interest expense of 26,544 USD m, so the net interest line depends on the fair value net interest line of 6,343 USD m as well (page:371). - Key figures: the underlying cost / income ratio was 74.4% and the reported ratio 81.1% (page:37). Underlying measures are non-GAAP, defined in the 20-F appendix and not rebuilt here. - Cash flow: net cash flow from operating activities was 21,851 USD m (3,279 USD m in FY2024); investing was an outflow of 22,802 USD m; financing was an outflow of 30,863 USD m; cash and cash equivalents ended the year at 231,375 USD m (pages:379 and 380). The net stable funding ratio was 116.1% against 125.5% (page:37). USD 51.8bn of assets were excluded from group high-quality liquid assets because they are effectively restricted in subsidiaries and branches (page:246). - Ratings sensitivity: on the ratings at 31.12.25, a one-notch downgrade would require USD 0.3bn of cash or collateral, two notches USD 0.6bn and three notches USD 0.9bn (page:245). The 2025 rating actions are an upgrade of Moody's long-term senior unsecured rating to A2 from A3 with a stable outlook, and Fitch outlook on the group's Long-Term Issuer Default Rating changed to Positive from Stable (page:245). The ratings in force at 2026-11-05 are Not supplied. - 2026 path (all management statements, rounded as spoken): CET1 ratio 14.7% at end March, 14.4% at end June and 14.7% at end September; CET1 leverage ratio 4.4%, 4.4% and 4.6%; liquidity coverage ratio 178%, 177% and 179%; net stable funding ratio 117%, 115% and 115%; total loss-absorbing capacity 198, 194 and 187 USD bn (Q1 call page:6; Q2 call page:5; Q3 call page:5). The 20-F ratio for liquidity is a fourth-quarter average of 64 data points; the transcripts do not state their averaging basis, so the 2026 liquidity coverage figures are not strictly comparable with the year-end figure. - UBS AG standalone fully applied CET1 ratio: 13.9% at end March (Q1 call page:6), 14.4% at end June (Q2 call page:5) and 14.5% at end September (Q3 call page:6, after a dividend accrual of 1.8 billion). This is a different perimeter from the group. - Management capital intentions: a current programme completed in Q3 with "4.8 billion dollars" repurchased year to date, 1.2 billion more intended over the next three months, and a year-end CET1 ratio guided "at or very close to our target of around 14%" (Q3 call pages:3 and 5). Distributions are therefore planned to move the ratio down from 14.7%.

facts.label: Third quarter 2026 evidence and subsequent events
facts.text: - Reported Q3 2026 (spoken, rounded): net profit 2.7 billion, earnings per share 85 cents, effective tax rate 24.7%, Group credit loss expense 114 million, integration costs 452 million, and a 346 million charge from the repurchase of around 10 billion of high-cost Credit Suisse liabilities (Q3 call pages:4 and 5). Underlying pre-tax profit 4.1 billion, up 14%, underlying return on CET1 capital 16.7% and underlying cost / income ratio 68.7%. These underlying figures are management measures with no reconciliation in the pack. - Division items affecting the reported result: Non-core and Legacy pre-tax profit of 360 million after "275 million of litigation charges", and a Group Items reported pre-tax loss of 740 million that includes 265 million of own credit and hedging losses (Q3 call page:9). - Integration: 13.2 billion of gross cost reductions delivered, with about 0.5 billion more expected in the fourth quarter and about 0.5 billion of integration-related expenses expected in the fourth quarter (Q3 call pages:4 and 5). - Swiss capital rules: Q1 call page:4 states the announced measures "would require UBS to hold around 22 billion in additional capital in CET1 terms", on top of 15 billion already needed from the Credit Suisse acquisition under existing regulations. The Q3 call (page:3) calls the September outcome in the Upper House "very concerning", and states that the ordinance affects capital from 1 January 2029 and new rules for foreign subsidiaries probably no earlier than late 2027 (page:14). These are management statements; the rule text is not supplied. - Credit Suisse AT1 litigation: the appeal decision is expected "not before Q1 of 2027" (Q3 call page:14). The 20-F states that the cumulative effects of acquired litigation "may have material adverse consequences for the combined Group" (page:113). Litigation provisions were 2,200 USD m and acquisition-related contingent liabilities 531 USD m at 31.12.25 (page:434); the 2026 provision level is Not supplied. - Filing events: capitalization 6-Ks filed 29 April, 29 July and 28 October 2026 and call transcripts filed 30 April, 30 July and 29 October 2026. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The pack describes a listed bank holding company whose main creditor-relevant change is the 2023 acquisition of Credit Suisse Group AG and the integration that management says will be substantially complete at the end of 2026. The group runs five divisions, of which Global Wealth Management and the Investment Bank carry most divisional profit, and non-interest income is the larger part of revenue. No sponsor or controlling owner is disclosed, and the only holders above 3% named in the 20-F are Norges Bank and BlackRock Inc., so sponsor-behaviour analysis reduces to documented capital-return conduct. The transaction set for 2025 and 2026 consists of disposals, entity mergers, capital instruments and a liability management action in the third quarter of 2026, for which the pack gives amounts and charges but no instrument terms. The Swiss capital proposals and the legacy litigation are the main credit uncertainties and are described but not quantified by any rule text or court document in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The defining transaction in the pack is the acquisition of Credit Suisse Group AG on 12 June 2023, after which UBS Group AG "succeeding by operation of Swiss law to all assets and liabilities of Credit Suisse Group AG" (20-F page:41). The 20-F states the acquisition followed a request from the Swiss Federal Department of Finance, the Swiss National Bank and FINMA (page:40). The consideration included UBS Group AG shares (treasury shares transferred, page:377) and the 20-F records negative goodwill of 27,264 USD m in FY2023 (page:371); no purchase agreement or term sheet is supplied, so deal terms beyond these statements are Not supplied. Integration is described as substantially complete at the end of 2026: UBS AG and Credit Suisse AG merged in May 2024, UBS Switzerland AG and Credit Suisse (Schweiz) AG in July 2024, and further US and EU entity mergers followed in 2025 (page:41). Management says all former Credit Suisse client migrations were complete in March 2026 (Q1 call page:3). Creditor mechanics: a simpler legal structure and decommissioned legacy systems reduce operational and resolution complexity, while the remaining Non-core and Legacy book and acquired litigation keep a tail of loss and cash-cost risk until wound down. The year-end 2026 completion claim is management language and not yet evidenced by a filed statement.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Disposals and exits around the transaction: the sale of Select Portfolio Servicing was completed in March 2025 with a gain of 97 USD m and a reduction of about USD 1.3bn in risk-weighted assets (20-F page:42); the 50% interest in Swisscard was sold to American Express with completion in January 2026, a subsequent event relative to the FY2025 period, with a gain expected in the first quarter of 2026 (page:42); the Q1 call attributes a limited tax charge to that gain (page:5); and the sale of O'Connor was completed in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 call page:8, and "the O'Connor exit" in Q3 call page:8). Prices for these disposals are not given except where stated. Management also reports the conversion of UBS Bank USA to a national bank charter (Q1 call page:3) with product roll-out expected in 2027 (Q3 call page:12).

facts.text: New debt issues and liability management: the pack does not list any individual new bond, with coupon, maturity, size or issuer; that detail is Not supplied. What it does show is (i) 2025 cash flows from issuance of debt designated at fair value and long-term debt at amortized cost of 131,476 USD m against repayments of 154,614 USD m (20-F page:379); (ii) in 2025, new issuances of AT1 capital instruments of USD 5.8 bn and a call of USD 3.2 bn equivalent of AT1 capital instruments, with loss-absorbing AT1 capital up by USD 3.5 bn to USD 19.9 bn (page:232); (iii) management's statement that the 2026 AT1 issuance plan was completed by mid-February 2026 (Q1 call page:6) and that further AT1 was pre-funded in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 call page:5); (iv) total debt issued of 343,922 USD m at 31.3.26, 343,551 USD m at 30.6.26 and 324,981 USD m at 30.9.26; and (v) a third-quarter 2026 liability management transaction, "the repurchase of around 10 billion of high-cost Credit Suisse liabilities", which produced a charge of 346 million (Q3 call page:4). The sources do not say which instruments were repurchased, at what price, whether by tender or in the market, or whether holders were treated pro rata, so creditor treatment of that action is Insufficient Information and no conclusion is drawn on it. Management links it to lower funding drag in Non-core and Legacy and support for net interest income, which is its characterisation.

facts.text: Capital returns act as a use of funds. The 20-F shows share repurchase programmes of USD 2,000 m each in 2024 and 2025 (page:377), an accrual of 3,449 USD m for the proposed 2025 dividend and a capital reserve of 3,000 USD m for expected 2026 repurchases (page:231). Management links the pace to maintaining a CET1 ratio of around 14% and to the Swiss Parliament's deliberations (Q2 call page:3). These are distributions funded from reported earnings and are conditioned on a stated capital ratio. The capital-return plan for 2027 is to be given with fourth quarter results (Q3 call page:3).

facts.label: Regulatory and capital-rule context
facts.text: - The 20-F states that proposed legislation would require deduction of investments in foreign subsidiaries of systemically important banks from CET1 capital, entering into force in 2028 at the earliest, with a 65% deduction in the first year rising by 5-percentage-point steps to 100% (page:88). - The company states: "We currently estimate that UBS AG would be required to hold additional CET1 capital of around USD 22bn if all capital measures were implemented as proposed by the Swiss Federal Council" and that this would raise UBS Group AG's CET1 ratio to around 18.5% from its target of around 14% (page:89). The Q1 call gives the same order of magnitude, "around 22 billion", on top of 15 billion already required (page:4). - The 20-F states FINMA's preferred resolution strategy is a single point of entry at UBS Group AG, with write-down of equity, AT1 and tier 2 and conversion of senior unsecured bonds of UBS Group AG to equity if required (page:84). This is a description of the stated strategy, not a legal interpretation of creditor ranking. - Credit Suisse AT1 litigation: cases lodged against FINMA over the AT1 write-down, with UBS Group AG a party as successor (20-F page:113); management says no decision is expected before the first quarter of 2027 (Q3 call page:14). Provisions are in the financial base handoff; no claim amount is supplied.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: - Revenue durability. Evidence: net interest income is 7,747 USD m of 49,573 USD m total revenues and Global Wealth Management earns recurring net fee income on fee-generating assets (20-F pages:409 and 49 to 50). Mechanic: revenue depends on market levels, client activity and asset flows more than on loan margins, so revenue moves with markets. Implication: debt service capacity for a group of this size rests on earnings volatility and capital buffers, not on contractual interest cover; the financial base handoff gives the capital and liquidity figures. A logged conflict that counters part of this: none on revenue; the headcount measure conflict only affects cost-per-head analysis. - Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: operating expenses of 40,197 USD m and a reported cost / income ratio of 81.1% for FY2025, with management targeting below 70% underlying by year-end 2026 (20-F pages:371, 37, 47). Mechanic: integration cost savings are the planned margin driver, but they require integration expenses (Q3 call page:5). Implication: the margin path depends on completing the integration; the target is management language and the cost-to-achieve conflict above limits how far the savings economics can be checked. - Concentration risk. Evidence: Switzerland provides 32% of revenue and 49% of non-current assets, and the wealth and bank divisions carry most divisional profit (20-F pages:410, 409). Mechanic: Swiss regulation, the Swiss economy and the Swiss capital rules touch both the largest region and the group's legal structure. Implication: a Swiss rule change has outsized effect on distributions and structure; the company's own estimate of around USD 22bn extra CET1 at the bank subsidiary is the size marker. - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder disclosed (20-F page:262) and capital returns tied to a ratio target. Mechanic: there is no sponsor incentive for debt-funded extraction, but shareholder distributions compete with capital builds. Implication: monitor distribution decisions against the Swiss rule outcome; no extraction behaviour is evidenced and no conclusion on willingness is drawn. - Key uncertainties. Swiss capital rules and timing; Credit Suisse AT1 and merger-law litigation; the unverified year-end integration completion; the unknown terms of the Q3 liability management; and ratings in force at the as-of date.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: UBS Group AG is, on the evidence supplied, a strong and well-capitalized bank credit whose main risks are regulatory and legacy rather than earnings or liquidity. The strongest support is capital and liquidity: at 31 December 2025 CET1 capital was USD 71,262 million, 14.44% of risk-weighted assets against a Swiss requirement of 10.63%; the liquidity coverage ratio averaged 182.6% in the fourth quarter of 2025; and management reports a CET1 ratio of 14.7% at 30 September 2026. The weakest point is the Swiss capital package, which the company estimates would need around USD 22bn of extra CET1 at UBS AG, alongside unquantified Credit Suisse litigation. The outcome turns on the final Swiss rules and on how management balances buybacks against capital building.

The weakest point is the Swiss capital package, which the company estimates would need around USD 22bn of extra CET1 at UBS AG, alongside unquantified Credit Suisse litigation. The outcome turns on the final Swiss rules and on how management balances buybacks against capital building.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: First, capital is the anchor of the view. At 31 December 2025 eligible CET1 capital of USD 71,262 million exceeded the Swiss requirement of USD 52,448 million by USD 18,814 million, and eligible going concern capital of USD 91,176 million exceeded its requirement of USD 73,955 million by USD 17,221 million (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:229). Gone concern loss-absorbing capacity of USD 96,130 million exceeded its requirement of USD 52,917 million by USD 43,213 million (same page). On the leverage basis the cushions are thinner: CET1 of 4.39% of the leverage ratio denominator against 3.50%, and going concern capital of 5.62% against 5.00%. The mechanism is that losses are absorbed by CET1 and additional tier 1 before subordinated and senior unsecured creditors, so these cushions are the first protection for debt holders (Analyst Interpretation).

The mechanism is that losses are absorbed by CET1 and additional tier 1 before subordinated and senior unsecured creditors, so these cushions are the first protection for debt holders (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Second, funding and liquidity reduce refinancing risk. Customer deposits were USD 788,367 million at 31 December 2025, about 49% of total assets of USD 1,617,427 million, and loans and advances to customers were about 83% of deposits. High-quality liquid assets averaged USD 331.6 billion in the fourth quarter of 2025 and the liquidity coverage ratio was 182.6% against a floor of 100%, with USD 51.8 billion of assets excluded from the group figure as restricted in subsidiaries. Debt issued at amortized cost and fair value due within 12 months was USD 113.7 billion on an undiscounted basis including interest, which is below high-quality liquid assets by a factor of about 2.9 (Analyst Interpretation; a simple comparison, not a regulatory measure). Management reports a liquidity coverage ratio of 179% and a net stable funding ratio of 115% for the third quarter of 2026 (Management Language, rounded, averaging basis not stated).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Third, earnings are recovering from a low base but remain market-sensitive. Operating profit before tax was USD 8,853 million in FY2025 against USD 6,821 million in FY2024, an increase of about 30%, and net interest income was only USD 7,747 million of USD 49,573 million total revenues, so about 84% of revenue is non-interest income from fees and trading (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:371 and page:409). The reported cost / income ratio was 81.1% in FY2025. Management says the underlying ratio was 68.7% in the third quarter of 2026 and targets below 70% at the 2026 exit (Management Language, not reconciled in the pack). Because fee and trading income move with markets, profit and capital generation are exposed to market conditions, which weakens earnings-based protection but is cushioned by the capital above (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fourth, the Swiss capital package is the largest identified risk. The 20-F states the company estimates UBS AG would need additional CET1 of around USD 22bn if all measures were implemented as proposed, which would raise the group CET1 ratio to around 18.5% from its target of around 14%, with a phase-in starting in 2028 at the earliest (Documentary Fact; 20-F page:88 and page:89). Management calls the September 2026 Upper House outcome very concerning (Management Language). The mechanism, in management's words, is that the capital would be trapped against foreign subsidiary investments, so it cannot support distributions or growth. The implication for creditors is mixed: a higher requirement strengthens loss absorption, but it can also reduce shareholder returns and prompt structural change whose effect on creditors is not assessable from the pack (Insufficient Information).

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Fifth, legacy exposures and resolution mechanics matter for the holding company's creditors. The 20-F describes a single point of entry resolution strategy at UBS Group AG involving write-down of equity, AT1 and tier 2 and conversion of senior unsecured bonds of UBS Group AG to equity if required, and records Credit Suisse AT1 litigation in which UBS Group AG is a party as successor (20-F page:84 and page:113). These are mechanics, not outcomes: no claim amount is supplied.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. A capital base well above requirements on all three Swiss measures (Documentary Fact), with management guiding to a CET1 ratio of around 14%. A deposit-led balance sheet with large high-quality liquid assets and a liquidity coverage ratio of 182.6% (Documentary Fact). A diversified revenue base across five divisions and four regions, with Switzerland at 32% of FY2025 revenue and the Americas at 36% (Documentary Fact). Earnings that improved in FY2025 and, on management's account, in 2026 (Documentary Fact and Management Language). No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, so sponsor extraction is not an evident risk (Analyst Interpretation; the evidence is an absence in a limited pack).

rows.label: UBS Group AG looks like a strong, well-capitalized and liquid bank credit. Its main risks come from the pending Swiss capital rules and legacy litigation, not from weak earnings or debt service.
Capital and loss-absorbing capacity sat well above Swiss requirements at the end of 2025.
Liquidity is large against near-term debt maturities.
The Swiss capital package could require around USD 22bn of extra CET1 at the bank subsidiary.
Operating profit rose about 30% in 2025, and management reports an underlying cost / income ratio of 68.7% for the third quarter of 2026.
Fundamental credit view: strong, well-capitalized, liquid; main risks regulatory and legacy
Business risk: diversified fee-led model, near-complete integration, no sponsor
Financial risk and liquidity: strong buffers, market-sensitive earnings
Swiss capital rules on foreign subsidiary investments
Credit Suisse legacy and AT1 litigation

columns.label: Why it matters and what it affects

rows.label: No 2026 interim financial statements, only capitalization tables and call transcripts; 2026 figures are rounded and partly underlying
Instrument-level debt terms (issuer, ranking, coupon, maturity, call, guarantor) and the Q3 2026 liability management terms
Swiss capital rule text and final timing; company estimate is the only size marker
Credit Suisse litigation amounts, including AT1 and merger-law claims
Ratings in force at the as-of date

limitations: Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

## Request
- Issuer: UBS Group AG (issuer id `ubs`), as of 2026-11-05, information cutoff 2026-11-05 (context). Reporting currency USD; current period Q3 2026; prior period FY2025.
- Run: `ubs-2026-11-05-credit_snapshot-host`, pathway `credit_snapshot`, requested modules CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (the launcher's `minimum` set). CP-0 runs first as their dependency.
- Execution: host session. The host read the pinned source text and wrote this answer. No provider was called.
- Question: can the supplied filings support CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, and what remains blocked?
- Assertion: SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. No credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion; no figure is normalized, reconciled or calculated here.

## Findings
### Reader summary

All four downstream analyses can proceed with stated limits. | Medium | The three quarterly reports themselves and the results slides are not in the pack, so current-quarter statements are not available. |

| Audited annual statements, debt notes, capital and liquidity sections are all present for the group. | Year-end balance sheet, funding and loss-absorbing capacity can be traced to the filing. | High |

### Readiness view

The supplied set is sufficient to start all four requested analyses, each with stated limitations, and none is blocked or conditional. The 20-F supplies audited consolidated statements, notes, capital, liquidity and legal-entity disclosure for the UBS Group AG consolidated group in USD under IFRS Accounting Standards. For 2026 the pack holds three one-table capitalization 6-Ks and three earnings-call transcripts, which are management statements and not the quarterly reports they refer to. Source sufficiency here does not mean downstream analysis is complete.

### Source register

- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited facts. page:2: "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025", "UBS Group AG Commission file number: 1-36764". page:3: "International Financial Reporting Standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board ☑".

- Structure: page:3 explains the cross-reference table: "Annual Report refers to the Annual Report 2025 of UBS Group AG annexed hereto, which forms an integral part hereof" and "Supplement refers to certain supplemental information contained in this forepart of the Form 20-F". Financial Statements are the consolidated statements of UBS Group AG.

- Statements located: income statement page:371 ("Income statement For the year ended USD m Note 31.12.25 31.12.24 31.12.23"), statement of comprehensive income page:372, balance sheet page:373 ("Balance sheet USD m Note 31.12.25 31.12.24 Assets"), statement of changes in equity page:374. The cash flow statement is at page:378 ("Statement of cash flows For the year ended USD m 31.12.25 31.12.24 31.12.23").

- Debt: page:432 "Note 15 Debt issued designated at fair value USD m 31.12.25 31.12.24" and "Note 16 Debt issued measured at amortized cost USD m 31.12.25 31.12.24"; page:433 "Subordinated debt" with "of which: eligible as high-trigger loss-absorbing additional tier 1 capital instruments". These are category tables.

- Capital, liquidity and ratings: total loss-absorbing capacity page:227 to page:234; liquidity and funding page:244 to page:247; ratings page:244 "Credit ratings Credit ratings can affect the cost and availability of funding" and page:245 "During 2025, rating agencies took the following actions regarding UBS Group AG’s ratings". Material cash requirements page:253.

- Resolution framework: page:84 "FINMA’s preferred strategy for UBS is a single point of entry (SPE) strategy involving write-down of the Group’s remaining equity and additional tier 1 (AT1) and tier 2 instruments, conversion of senior unsecured bonds of UBS Group AG to equity, if required".

- Legal entities: page:515 "Note 27 Interests in subsidiaries and other entities a) Interests in subsidiaries". Significant regulated subsidiary and sub-group data page:532 and page:535 ("UBS Switzerland AG (standalone) UBS Europe SE (consolidated) UBS Americas Holding LLC (consolidated)"; "Credit Suisse International (standalone)").

- Litigation and contingencies: page:113 ("numerous cases have been lodged against the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) in respect of the write-down of the Credit Suisse Group’s additional tier 1 (AT1) bonds"); provisions and contingent liabilities discussed from page:434 to page:449.
- Auditor: page:14 "Independent Auditors Ernst & Young Ltd , Aeschengraben 27, 4051 Basel, Switzerland , PCAOB number 1460".

- Extraction gap on the audit reports: page:371 says "The accompanying reports of the independent registered public accounting firm ... are included in our filing on 9 March 2026 with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Form 20-F". It is followed only by running headers "Consolidated financial statements 241 Annual Report 2025 | Financial statements | Consolidated financial statements 242" through 245, with no opinion text. The audit opinion wording is therefore not located in the pinned text. Page:370 does state that management's internal control assessment was audited and "expresses an unqualified opinion", which is a description of the opinion, not the opinion itself.
- Units: USD millions in the statements (page:373 "USD m"). Printed page numbers (for example 248) are annual-report pages; the locators in this answer are extraction chunks.
#### Capitalization 6-Ks (three files)

- Family and authority: filed 6-K extracts furnished for registration-statement incorporation. Q1 file page:2: "Capitalization of UBS Group AG The table below presents the consolidated capitalization of UBS Group AG in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards in US dollars, the presentation currency of UBS Group AG."
- Q1 file (page:2) has the only short-term versus long-term split: "Short-term debt issued 1 97,642 92,096 Long-term debt issued 2 246,279 236,405", and the high-trigger AT1 subline.

- Q2 file (page:1) and Q3 file (page:1) show a single line: "Debt issued 1 343,551 343,922" and "Debt issued 1,2 324,981 343,551". The short-term and long-term split is not repeated, and the footnote definitions differ between files. The Q3 file's footnote reads "As of 30 September 2026, 87% of Debt issued was unsecured."
- Perimeter: consolidated UBS Group AG, USD. The Q1 footnote defines debt as issued "by UBS Group AG and its subsidiaries", so it is not holding-company-only debt.
- Naming: the file-name date (for example 2026-03-31) is the report period, not the filing date; the printed cover dates are 29 April, 29 July and 28 October 2026.
- Authority: these tables are filed issuer disclosure, but they are only a capitalization extract. They carry no income statement, cash flow, capital ratio or liquidity data.
#### Earnings-call transcripts (three files)

- Family and authority: management speeches and analyst Q&A furnished on 6-K, attributed supporting claims and not financial statements. Q3 file page:2: "This Form 6-K consists of the transcripts of the of UBS Group 3Q26 Earnings call remarks and Analyst Q&A". Co-registrants: "UBS Group AG ... Commission File Number: 1-36764" and "UBS AG ... Commission File Number: 1-15060". The transcript perimeter is therefore the group, with some UBS AG standalone remarks.

- Slides are not supplied. page:2 of each file: "Numbers for slides refer to the third quarter 2026 results presentation" (and the first and second quarter equivalents). Slide-level tables, charts and footnotes cannot be inspected; only spoken text is present.

- Content located in the Q3 file: group results and capital ratios page:4 to page:5 ("Our CET1 capital ratio at the end of September was 14.7%"; "total loss-absorbing capacity of 187 billion, a net stable funding ratio of 115% and an LCR of 179%"); division results page:6 to page:9; Swiss capital-rule discussion page:3 to page:4 ("September’s outcome in the Upper House is very concerning") and Q&A page:10 to page:14; Credit Suisse AT1 litigation timing page:14 ("decision not before Q1 of 2027"); UBS AG standalone capital page:5 to page:6.

- Q1 and Q2 files cover the same structure for their quarters (page:2 onward); Q2 page:5 carries "a net stable funding ratio of 115% and an LCR of 177%" and "Our CET1 capital ratio at the end of June was 14.4%".
- Currency: the speakers mix USD and CHF (for example Personal & Corporate Banking is stated in Swiss francs, Q3 file page:7). Any figure used must carry its stated currency.
### Information-availability boundary
- Every supplied source is dated on or before 29 October 2026, before the as-of date and cutoff of 2026-11-05. Nothing in the pack is dated after the cutoff.
- Nothing dated between 29 October 2026 and 5 November 2026 is supplied. Events in that window are Not supplied, not absent.

- The Q3 transcript mentions future events (a fourth-quarter results update and a strategic update, a 2027 capital-return plan, Swiss parliamentary deliberations). These are management statements about the future, not facts as of the cutoff.
### Identity and perimeter
- Reporting entity: UBS Group AG, Switzerland, consolidated, IFRS Accounting Standards, presentation currency USD (6-K Q1 page:2 above; 20-F page:3).

- Related entities named in the sources: UBS AG (co-registrant on the transcripts, page:2; standalone CET1 discussed Q3 page:5 to page:6), UBS Switzerland AG, UBS Europe SE, UBS Americas Holding LLC, Credit Suisse International (20-F page:532, page:535), and Credit Suisse Group AG and Credit Suisse AG as former entities (20-F page:38 definitions). The sources describe UBS Group AG as the holding company in the resolution strategy (page:84). Which entity issued which instrument, and who guarantees what, is Unresolved from category-level debt tables; the guarantor field in the context is blank, which is not evidence of none.

- Segment and consolidation differences: 20-F page:532 shows significant regulated subsidiaries and sub-groups on their own bases ("Swiss SRB rules", "EU regulatory rules", "US Basel III rules"), which differ from the group IFRS statements. Do not mix these perimeters.

- Bank sector note: this is a deposit-taking bank holding group (customer deposits are the main liability on page:373). The method's industrial-style debt, leverage and covenant analysis does not map directly; the relevant measures are regulatory capital, total loss-absorbing capacity and liquidity ratios, which the sources do contain. This is a note on source fit, not a conclusion.
### Consumer evidence demand
| Consumer | Evidence it needs | Located | Limitation carried forward |

| CP-1 | Annual and interim statements, debt, liquidity, capital, non-GAAP measures | 20-F page:371 to page:374 and page:378 (statements), page:432 to page:433 (debt), page:227 to page:247 (capital and liquidity); capitalization tables for the three 2026 quarter-ends; transcripts for 2026 quarterly commentary | No quarterly report or interim statements; no results slides; "underlying" and adjusted measures in the transcripts have no reconciliation in the pack |

| CP-1A | Business, divisions, history, integration, ownership, transactions | 20-F cross-reference page:3 to page:5 and business sections cited there; transcripts for divisional commentary and integration status | Credit Suisse integration and regulatory narrative is management-attributed; no shareholder register or transaction documents |

| CP-2 | Capital structure, debt by instrument, maturities, ranking, covenants, liquidity | 20-F debt notes page:432 to page:433; maturity analysis cited at page:253; capitalization tables | Instrument-level terms, indentures, maturities by issue and guarantor structure not supplied; no covenant concept appears in the sources at the level of an industrial credit agreement |
| CP-5 | Traceable claims | Every source has stable chunk numbers | Text extraction only; slides, charts and audit reports are not evidenced |
### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: the 20-F gives audited FY2025 statements with FY2024 comparatives (and FY2023 for the income statement and cash flows), with notes, and sections on capital, loss-absorbing capacity, liquidity and funding, ratings actions, resolution strategy, subsidiaries and litigation. It is enough to build a reported financial foundation for FY2025 on the group perimeter.

- Strongest contrary evidence: the evidence for Q3 2026 is thin. The quarterly reports referred to on the 6-K covers ("UBS Group AG’s third quarter 2026 report, submitted to the SEC on Form 6-K on October 28, 2026", Q3 capitalization file page:1) are named but not supplied. The only Q3 balance-sheet line in a filed table is the capitalization extract. Every Q3 earnings, capital and liquidity figure therefore rests on transcript speech. A management claim cannot override the 20-F, and it has no filed statement to reconcile against in this pack.

- Source risk mechanism: the capitalization tables change presentation between the Q1 file (short-term and long-term split) and the Q2 and Q3 files (single debt line), so a consumer that wants maturity profile at Q3 cannot take it from the supplied tables; the consequence is that the 2026 maturity split stops at 31.3.26 and must be labelled as stale for later quarters. Debt notes in the 20-F are by category (senior unsecured, covered bonds, subordinated, Swiss central mortgage institutions), so a consumer that needs instrument-level ranking or issuer must mark it Not supplied.

- What cannot proceed: instrument-level capital structure and covenant analysis; interim statement tables for 2026; slide-based charts; audit opinion wording; quantified effect of pending Swiss capital rules (the transcripts discuss alternatives without a supplied rule text).

- Next evidence action: supply the first, second and third quarter 2026 reports (the documents the capitalization 6-Ks point to), the results presentations, the 20-F audit reports, and any prospectus supplements or Pillar 3 report that list individual debt and capital instruments.
## Calculations
No new calculation. CP-0 does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. Figures quoted above are shown only as exact substrings of the sources, to locate them.
## Gaps

| First, second and third quarter 2026 reports (income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, notes) are not supplied; only capitalization extracts and call transcripts | High | CP-1, CP-2, CP-5 | Supply the three quarterly reports referenced on the capitalization 6-K covers |
| Results presentations (slides) are not supplied; the transcripts refer to slide numbers | Medium | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-5 | Supply the slide decks for the three quarters |

| Transcript "underlying" and adjusted measures have no reconciliation to reported figures in the pack | Medium | CP-1 | Supply the quarterly reports with their reconciliations |

| Swiss capital-rule proposals and Credit Suisse AT1 litigation are narrative only; rule text, court filings and provision amounts for 2026 are not supplied | Medium | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply the proposals, and the quarterly litigation note when available |
| Events from 29 October 2026 to 5 November 2026 are not supplied | Low | CP-1A, CP-2 | Supply later 6-Ks or confirm none |
| Credit rating levels as of the as-of date are not supplied; the 20-F reports 2025 actions and the context has no ratings | Medium | CP-2 | Supply current agency reports |

## Next module

- CP-1: use the 20-F statements (page:371 to page:374) as controlling for FY2025. Treat the transcripts as attributed management claims. Keep the group perimeter separate from UBS AG and the significant subsidiaries. Label every Q3 2026 figure by its source type and currency. Do not draw a short-term and long-term debt split after 31.3.26 from the supplied tables.

- Perimeter: UBS Group AG consolidated, IFRS Accounting Standards, USD, unless a row says otherwise. UBS AG and other subsidiaries are named only where a source reports them separately.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The audited 2025 statements show a very large, deposit-funded bank balance sheet with capital and liquidity ratios above the stated requirements. Third-quarter 2026 evidence is management commentary plus a debt and equity table. | Medium | There are no interim financial statements for 2026, so current-quarter figures are rounded spoken claims. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Customer deposits are the largest funding source, with debt issued second. | Funding is mostly deposit based, while debt issued is a separate wholesale layer that includes subordinated and loss-absorbing instruments. | High |

| The common equity tier 1 ratio was 14.4% at year-end 2025 and 14.7% at the end of September 2026 on management's figure. | Capital sits above the management target of around 14%, and management guides the ratio back toward that level by year-end after buyback accruals. | Medium |

| Debt issued fell between mid-2026 and end of September 2026 in the capitalization table. | A lower debt stock is visible, but the table gives no maturity split or instrument detail for that date. | Medium |
| Swiss capital proposals and Credit Suisse legacy litigation are unquantified in the pack. | These can raise capital needs or cash costs, and their size cannot be measured from the sources. | Low |
### Financial base view

The supplied sources support a reported financial base for UBS Group AG on one audited year and one interim indicator set. FY2025 is fully audited and cross-checks to the key-figures table: revenues, expenses, profit, balance sheet, cash flow, capital, liquidity and debt notes all tie within rounding. For 2026 the pack holds only a capitalization table per quarter and call transcripts, so Q3 2026 figures other than debt issued and equity are management claims, stated rounded, with underlying measures that are not reconciled in the pack. The financial base is therefore firm for FY2025 and FY2024 and indicative only for Q3 2026. These sources report no EBITDA, no committed undrawn revolving facility and no covenant package, so industrial leverage, interest cover and facility liquidity metrics are Not supplied, and regulatory capital, loss-absorbing capacity and liquidity ratios carry the analysis.

### Source context and perimeter

- Entity and basis: the 20-F covers UBS Group AG consolidated. Income statement page:371 is headed "Income statement For the year ended USD m Note 31.12.25 31.12.24 31.12.23", the balance sheet page:373 is "Balance sheet USD m Note 31.12.25 31.12.24", and the basis is IFRS Accounting Standards (page:3). All statements are in USD millions.

- Ownership: "UBS Group AG owns 100% of the outstanding shares in UBS AG" (20-F page:36). UBS AG standalone, UBS Switzerland AG, UBS Europe SE and UBS Americas Holding LLC report separately on regulatory bases (page:532) and are not part of the consolidated rows above.

- Capitalization table authority: filed 6-K tables, group consolidated, USD. The Q1 file (page:2) defines debt as issued "by UBS Group AG and its subsidiaries", and the later files (page:1 each) define debt issued as the sum of "Debt issued measured at amortized cost and Debt issued designated at fair value".

- Call transcripts are attributed management speech. They are not financial statements and do not override the 20-F; where a transcript figure and a filed table could be compared, they are compared below.
- Currency: group figures are USD. Division figures in the calls may be in Swiss francs (for example Personal & Corporate Banking, Q3 call page:7); none are used as group figures here.
### Audited FY2025 results

- Revenues were 49,573 USD m, up from 48,611 USD m in FY2024 (an increase of 962). Operating expenses fell from 41,239 USD m to 40,197 USD m. Credit loss expense was 524 USD m against 551 USD m (page:371).

- Operating profit before tax rose from 6,821 USD m to 8,853 USD m; the tax expense was 1,056 USD m, giving net profit of 7,797 USD m, of which 7,767 USD m is attributable to shareholders (pages:371 and 372). FY2023 operating profit of 28,255 USD m included negative goodwill of 27,264 USD m from the Credit Suisse acquisition (page:371), so FY2023 is not a run-rate comparative.

- The income statement mix is: net interest income 7,747 USD m, other net income from financial instruments at fair value through profit or loss 14,011 USD m, net fee and commission income 27,912 USD m and other income of negative 96 USD m (page:371). Interest income from amortized cost and fair value through other comprehensive income instruments was 27,948 USD m against interest expense of 26,544 USD m, so the net interest line depends on the fair value net interest line of 6,343 USD m as well (page:371).
- Key figures: the underlying cost / income ratio was 74.4% and the reported ratio 81.1% (page:37). Underlying measures are non-GAAP, defined in the 20-F appendix and not rebuilt here.

- Cash flow: net cash flow from operating activities was 21,851 USD m (3,279 USD m in FY2024); investing was an outflow of 22,802 USD m; financing was an outflow of 30,863 USD m; cash and cash equivalents ended the year at 231,375 USD m (pages:379 and 380). For a bank, operating cash flow is dominated by changes in loans, deposits and trading balances, so it is not a free cash flow measure.
### Balance sheet, funding and debt

- Total assets were 1,617,427 USD m at 31.12.25 against 1,565,028 USD m, an increase of 52,399. Customer deposits were 788,367 USD m against 745,777 USD m (page:373). Of customer deposits, 259,372 USD m were demand deposits and 256,764 USD m time deposits (page:432).

- Debt issued: amortized cost 214,706 USD m (page:433) plus designated at fair value 113,794 USD m (page:432). The fair value debt is 100% unsecured and is dominated by structured instruments (equity-linked 60,303 USD m).

- Amortized cost debt: short-term debt 33,870 USD m; senior unsecured debt 122,574 USD m of which 89,739 USD m contributes to total loss-absorbing capacity and 24,648 USD m is issued by UBS AG standalone with original maturity above one year; covered bonds 11,651 USD m; subordinated debt 17,878 USD m; debt issued through the Swiss central mortgage institutions 28,278 USD m; other long-term debt 456 USD m (pages:432 and 433).

- Subordination: of subordinated debt, 17,551 USD m is high-trigger loss-absorbing additional tier 1 and 207 USD m non-Basel III-compliant tier 2; "All of the subordinated debt instruments outstanding as of 31 December 2025 pay a fixed rate of interest" (page:433).

- Security: covered bonds and the Swiss mortgage institution debt are 100% secured and other long-term debt 97% secured; everything else is unsecured (page:433). The capitalization tables state 88% of debt issued unsecured at 31.3.26 and 30.6.26, and 87% at 30.9.26 (page:2 of the Q1 file, page:1 of the Q2 file and page:1 of the Q3 file).

- Guarantee found in the 20-F: "UBS Group AG, together with UBS AG, has fully and unconditionally guaranteed the outstanding US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)-registered debt securities of Credit Suisse (USA) LLC", a single issuance of 742 USD m maturing July 2032 (page:433).

- 2026 debt: the Q1 file shows short-term debt issued of 97,642 USD m and long-term of 246,279 USD m at 31.3.26 (page:2). Total debt issued was 343,922 USD m at 31.3.26, 343,551 USD m at 30.6.26 and 324,981 USD m at 30.9.26. The Q3 transcript links part of Q3 activity to "the repurchase of around 10 billion of high-cost Credit Suisse liabilities" (page:4), but it does not say how much of the fall in the table this explains, and currency effects are not split out.
### Debt maturity profile (FY2025, undiscounted, USD bn)

The 20-F reports the maturity of debt issued measured at amortized cost on an undiscounted basis including future interest (page:497): due within 1 month 9.4, 1 to 3 months 9.1, 3 to 12 months 46.8, 1 to 2 years 25.7, 2 to 5 years 66.5, over 5 years 82.6, perpetual or not applicable 17.6, total 257.6. For debt designated at fair value the buckets are 14.4, 10.6, 23.4, 31.5, 13.1 and 41.5, total 134.4 (page:497). The perpetual bucket holds AT1 instruments with interest counted over five years (page:498 footnote 2). The profile is by time bucket, not by year, and not by instrument; a maturity wall by calendar year is Not supplied. Calculated 12-month totals are in Calculations.
### Capital, loss-absorbing capacity and liquidity

- Capital at 31.12.25 (Swiss systemically relevant bank framework): CET1 capital 71,262 USD m, risk-weighted assets 493,397 USD m, CET1 ratio 14.4%, going concern capital ratio 18.5%, total loss-absorbing capacity ratio 38.0%, leverage ratio denominator 1,622,438 USD m and CET1 leverage ratio 4.4% (page:37). Requirements: going concern capital 14.99% of risk-weighted assets and 5.00% of leverage ratio denominator; CET1 10.63% and 3.50%; eligible going concern capital 18.48% and 5.62% (page:229).

- Liquidity at 4Q25 average: high-quality liquid assets 331.6 USD bn, net cash outflows 181.7 USD bn, liquidity coverage ratio 182.6% against 188.4% in 4Q24 (page:246). The net stable funding ratio was 116.1% against 125.5% (page:37). USD 51.8bn of assets were excluded from group high-quality liquid assets because they are effectively restricted in subsidiaries and branches (page:246).

- Ratings sensitivity: on the ratings at 31.12.25, a one-notch downgrade would require USD 0.3bn of cash or collateral, two notches USD 0.6bn and three notches USD 0.9bn (page:245). The 2025 rating actions are an upgrade of Moody's long-term senior unsecured rating to A2 from A3 with a stable outlook, and Fitch outlook on the group's Long-Term Issuer Default Rating changed to Positive from Stable (page:245). The ratings in force at 2026-11-05 are Not supplied.

- 2026 path (all management statements, rounded as spoken): CET1 ratio 14.7% at end March, 14.4% at end June and 14.7% at end September; CET1 leverage ratio 4.4%, 4.4% and 4.6%; liquidity coverage ratio 178%, 177% and 179%; net stable funding ratio 117%, 115% and 115%; total loss-absorbing capacity 198, 194 and 187 USD bn (Q1 call page:6; Q2 call page:5; Q3 call page:5). The 20-F ratio for liquidity is a fourth-quarter average of 64 data points; the transcripts do not state their averaging basis, so the 2026 liquidity coverage figures are not strictly comparable with the year-end figure.

- UBS AG standalone fully applied CET1 ratio: 13.9% at end March (Q1 call page:6), 14.4% at end June (Q2 call page:5) and 14.5% at end September (Q3 call page:6, after a dividend accrual of 1.8 billion). This is a different perimeter from the group.

- Management capital intentions: a current programme completed in Q3 with "4.8 billion dollars" repurchased year to date, 1.2 billion more intended over the next three months, and a year-end CET1 ratio guided "at or very close to our target of around 14%" (Q3 call pages:3 and 5). Distributions are therefore planned to move the ratio down from 14.7%.
### Third quarter 2026 evidence and subsequent events

- Reported Q3 2026 (spoken, rounded): net profit 2.7 billion, earnings per share 85 cents, effective tax rate 24.7%, Group credit loss expense 114 million, integration costs 452 million, and a 346 million charge from the repurchase of around 10 billion of high-cost Credit Suisse liabilities (Q3 call pages:4 and 5). Underlying pre-tax profit 4.1 billion, up 14%, underlying return on CET1 capital 16.7% and underlying cost / income ratio 68.7%. These underlying figures are management measures with no reconciliation in the pack.

- Division items affecting the reported result: Non-core and Legacy pre-tax profit of 360 million after "275 million of litigation charges", and a Group Items reported pre-tax loss of 740 million that includes 265 million of own credit and hedging losses (Q3 call page:9).

- Integration: 13.2 billion of gross cost reductions delivered, with about 0.5 billion more expected in the fourth quarter and about 0.5 billion of integration-related expenses expected in the fourth quarter (Q3 call pages:4 and 5).

- Swiss capital rules: Q1 call page:4 states the announced measures "would require UBS to hold around 22 billion in additional capital in CET1 terms", on top of 15 billion already needed from the Credit Suisse acquisition under existing regulations. The Q3 call (page:3) calls the September outcome in the Upper House "very concerning", and states that the ordinance affects capital from 1 January 2029 and new rules for foreign subsidiaries probably no earlier than late 2027 (page:14). These are management statements; the rule text is not supplied.

- Credit Suisse AT1 litigation: the appeal decision is expected "not before Q1 of 2027" (Q3 call page:14). The 20-F states that the cumulative effects of acquired litigation "may have material adverse consequences for the combined Group" (page:113). Litigation provisions were 2,200 USD m and acquisition-related contingent liabilities 531 USD m at 31.12.25 (page:434); the 2026 provision level is Not supplied.

- Filing events: capitalization 6-Ks filed 29 April, 29 July and 28 October 2026 and call transcripts filed 30 April, 30 July and 29 October 2026. Nothing in the pack is dated after 29 October 2026; events from 30 October to 5 November 2026 are Not supplied.
### Definition risks

- Underlying versus reported: the 20-F reports an underlying cost / income ratio of 74.4% and a reported ratio of 81.1% for FY2025 (page:37); the Q3 underlying ratio of 68.7% is on the same management concept but is not reconciled in the pack.
- Debt issued is a group-wide measure covering the holding company and all subsidiaries, including structured notes at fair value. It is not holding-company debt and not an index-eligible bond count.
- Liquidity and capital ratios use the Swiss framework and different averaging bases; they are not comparable with ratios from other jurisdictions.

- The capitalization tables switch from a short-term and long-term split at 31.3.26 to a single line from 30.6.26, and the footnote wording changes, so a debt stock series by maturity class is not available after 31.3.26.
- Rounding: the pack's sub-totals carry differences of 1 USD m, shown in Calculations.
### Corrections to the readiness handoff

- The readiness handoff recorded guarantor structure as unresolved from category-level debt tables. The 20-F does disclose one guarantee: UBS Group AG and UBS AG guarantee the SEC-registered debt of Credit Suisse (USA) LLC (page:433). The wider guarantor mapping by instrument is still not supplied.
- The readiness handoff treated UBS Group AG as the holding company on the basis of the resolution description; the 20-F also states directly that it owns 100% of UBS AG (page:36).

## Request
- Issuer: UBS Group AG (issuer id `ubs`), as of 2026-11-05, information cutoff 2026-11-05. Reporting currency USD; current period Q3 2026; prior period FY2025.
- Question: which transaction, business, ownership and operating facts matter most to a creditor of UBS Group AG, and what do they mean through to credit implications?
- Perimeter: UBS Group AG consolidated unless a row names UBS AG or another entity. The context names no borrower, parent, sponsor or guarantor; blank fields are not evidence of none.

- Prohibited and not done here: peer ranking, instrument recommendation and recovery conclusion. Category tags follow the method: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation, Insufficient Information.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| UBS Group AG is a listed Swiss bank holding company with no sponsor or controlling holder disclosed. Its credit context is the Credit Suisse integration, a diversified fee-led model, and a pending Swiss capital-rule change that management opposes. | Medium | Transaction detail, new debt terms and the Swiss rule text are not in the pack; most 2026 facts are management statements. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Wealth management and the investment bank generate most divisional profit, and most revenue is not net interest income. | Earnings depend on fees and trading, so market conditions affect revenue durability more than lending margins do. | High |

| The 2023 Credit Suisse acquisition is nearly integrated, with cost savings and legacy wind-down on management's schedule. | Remaining execution, litigation and legacy exposure risks should fall, but the end state is a management claim until year-end. | Medium |

| Proposed Swiss rules would deduct foreign-subsidiary investments from capital; the company estimates about USD 22bn of extra CET1 at the bank subsidiary. | A large capital need could limit distributions or force structural change, but timing and final rules are unresolved. | Medium |

| No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed; documented actions are capital returns within a stated ratio target. | Sponsor-style extraction or priming is not evidenced, but missing evidence is not proof it cannot happen. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

The pack describes a listed bank holding company whose main creditor-relevant change is the 2023 acquisition of Credit Suisse Group AG and the integration that management says will be substantially complete at the end of 2026. The group runs five divisions, of which Global Wealth Management and the Investment Bank carry most divisional profit, and non-interest income is the larger part of revenue. No sponsor or controlling owner is disclosed, and the only holders above 3% named in the 20-F are Norges Bank and BlackRock Inc., so sponsor-behaviour analysis reduces to documented capital-return conduct. The transaction set for 2025 and 2026 consists of disposals, entity mergers, capital instruments and a liability management action in the third quarter of 2026, for which the pack gives amounts and charges but no instrument terms. The Swiss capital proposals and the legacy litigation are the main credit uncertainties and are described but not quantified by any rule text or court document in the pack.
### Company and operating model
| Fact | Category | Detail | Source and limitation |

| Divisional structure | Documentary Fact | Five business divisions plus Group functions: Global Wealth Management, Personal & Corporate Banking, Asset Management, the Investment Bank, and Non-core and Legacy; all five are reportable segments | 20-F page:407 |

| Global Wealth Management scale | Documentary Fact | FY2025 total revenues 25,960 USD m, operating profit before tax 5,207 USD m; invested assets USD 4.8trn of which fee-generating USD 2.1trn; lending portfolio USD 327bn; deposits USD 479bn at 31.12.25 | 20-F page:409 and page:49 to page:50 |

| Global Wealth Management revenue model | Documentary Fact | Recurring net fee income linked to fee-generating assets, plus transaction-based income and net interest income from lending and deposits | 20-F page:49 to page:50; Q3 call page:7 gives the Q3 2026 mix as management language |

| Personal & Corporate Banking | Documentary Fact | FY2025 total revenues 9,154 USD m, net interest income 5,322 USD m, operating profit before tax 2,497 USD m; Swiss retail, corporate and institutional business | 20-F page:409 and page:407 |
| Asset Management | Documentary Fact | FY2025 total revenues 3,156 USD m, operating profit before tax 719 USD m | 20-F page:409 |

| Investment Bank | Documentary Fact | FY2025 total revenues 12,340 USD m, operating profit before tax 2,819 USD m; net interest income of negative 2,938 USD m | 20-F page:409; the negative net interest line is shown as printed and its cause (funding cost allocation) is not stated in the cited pages |

| Non-core and Legacy and Group Items | Documentary Fact | Non-core and Legacy: revenues 154 USD m, loss before tax of 1,199 USD m; Group Items: loss before tax of 1,190 USD m | 20-F page:409; Non-core and Legacy holds selected former Credit Suisse positions not aligned with long-term priorities (page:407) |

| Revenue mix | Analyst Interpretation | Net interest income 7,747 USD m against non-interest income 41,826 USD m, so revenue is mainly fees and trading rather than net interest | 20-F page:409; share calculated in Calculations |
| Geography | Documentary Fact | FY2025 revenue share: Americas 36%, Asia Pacific 16%, EMEA excluding Switzerland 17%, Switzerland 32%; Switzerland holds 49% of non-current assets | 20-F page:410 |
| Cost structure | Documentary Fact | Personnel expenses 27,861 USD m, general and administrative 8,807 USD m, depreciation, amortization and impairment 3,529 USD m | 20-F page:371 |
| Capital spending | Documentary Fact | Purchase of property, equipment and software 2,362 USD m in FY2025 | 20-F page:379 |

| Management ambitions | Management Language | 2026 exit-rate targets: underlying return on CET1 capital of around 15% and underlying cost / income ratio below 70%; 2028 ambition: reported return on CET1 of around 18% | 20-F page:47 to page:48; targets, not results |

| Integration savings progress | Management Language | Cumulative gross cost savings 10.7bn at the end of 2025, 13.2bn delivered by Q3 2026 and about 13.7bn expected in total | 20-F page:41; Q3 call pages:4 and 5; management claims |

| Q3 2026 trading state | Management Language | Management calls Q3 2026 a strong quarter with year-on-year profit growth in each division and a record third quarter for the Investment Bank | Q3 call pages:2 to 9; no segment statements for Q3 2026 in the pack |
### Company profile

| Listing | Documentary Fact | Ordinary shares listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange and the New York Stock Exchange; ticker UBS | 20-F page:36 and page:2 |
| Reporting basis | Documentary Fact | IFRS Accounting Standards, USD presentation currency | 20-F page:3; capitalization 6-Ks page:2 and page:1 |

| Ownership class | Documentary Fact | No controlling holder or sponsor disclosed. Holders above 3% of voting rights at 31 December 2025: Norges Bank 4.90% (disclosed 22 January 2025) and BlackRock Inc. 5.01% (disclosed 30 November 2023) | 20-F page:262; Norges Bank disclosed a holding below 3% on 17 February 2026; the BlackRock notice is dated 2023 and may be stale |

| Control rights and economic interest | Insufficient Information | Voting and economic rights beyond one vote per share are not described in the pages read; percentages for other holders are not disclosed | Not inferred |

| Capital guidance | Management Language | Maintain a CET1 ratio of around 14%, a CET1 leverage ratio above 4.0% and a UBS AG standalone CET1 ratio of between 12.5% and 13.0% | 20-F page:48 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The defining transaction in the pack is the acquisition of Credit Suisse Group AG on 12 June 2023, after which UBS Group AG "succeeding by operation of Swiss law to all assets and liabilities of Credit Suisse Group AG" (20-F page:41). The 20-F states the acquisition followed a request from the Swiss Federal Department of Finance, the Swiss National Bank and FINMA (page:40). The consideration included UBS Group AG shares (treasury shares transferred, page:377) and the 20-F records negative goodwill of 27,264 USD m in FY2023 (page:371); no purchase agreement or term sheet is supplied, so deal terms beyond these statements are Not supplied. Integration is described as substantially complete at the end of 2026: UBS AG and Credit Suisse AG merged in May 2024, UBS Switzerland AG and Credit Suisse (Schweiz) AG in July 2024, and further US and EU entity mergers followed in 2025 (page:41). Management says all former Credit Suisse client migrations were complete in March 2026 (Q1 call page:3). Creditor mechanics: a simpler legal structure and decommissioned legacy systems reduce operational and resolution complexity, while the remaining Non-core and Legacy book and acquired litigation keep a tail of loss and cash-cost risk until wound down. The year-end 2026 completion claim is management language and not yet evidenced by a filed statement.

Disposals and exits around the transaction: the sale of Select Portfolio Servicing was completed in March 2025 with a gain of 97 USD m and a reduction of about USD 1.3bn in risk-weighted assets (20-F page:42); the 50% interest in Swisscard was sold to American Express with completion in January 2026, a subsequent event relative to the FY2025 period, with a gain expected in the first quarter of 2026 (page:42); the Q1 call attributes a limited tax charge to that gain (page:5); and the sale of O'Connor was completed in the first quarter of 2026 (Q1 call page:8, and "the O'Connor exit" in Q3 call page:8). Prices for these disposals are not given except where stated. Management also reports the conversion of UBS Bank USA to a national bank charter (Q1 call page:3) with product roll-out expected in 2027 (Q3 call page:12).

New debt issues and liability management: the pack does not list any individual new bond, with coupon, maturity, size or issuer; that detail is Not supplied. What it does show is (i) 2025 cash flows from issuance of debt designated at fair value and long-term debt at amortized cost of 131,476 USD m against repayments of 154,614 USD m (20-F page:379); (ii) in 2025, new issuances of AT1 capital instruments of USD 5.8 bn and a call of USD 3.2 bn equivalent of AT1 capital instruments, with loss-absorbing AT1 capital up by USD 3.5 bn to USD 19.9 bn (page:232); (iii) management's statement that the 2026 AT1 issuance plan was completed by mid-February 2026 (Q1 call page:6) and that further AT1 was pre-funded in the second quarter of 2026 (Q2 call page:5); (iv) total debt issued of 343,922 USD m at 31.3.26, 343,551 USD m at 30.6.26 and 324,981 USD m at 30.9.26; and (v) a third-quarter 2026 liability management transaction, "the repurchase of around 10 billion of high-cost Credit Suisse liabilities", which produced a charge of 346 million (Q3 call page:4). The sources do not say which instruments were repurchased, at what price, whether by tender or in the market, or whether holders were treated pro rata, so creditor treatment of that action is Insufficient Information and no conclusion is drawn on it. Management links it to lower funding drag in Non-core and Legacy and support for net interest income, which is its characterisation.

Capital returns act as a use of funds. The 20-F shows share repurchase programmes of USD 2,000 m each in 2024 and 2025 (page:377), an accrual of 3,449 USD m for the proposed 2025 dividend and a capital reserve of 3,000 USD m for expected 2026 repurchases (page:231). In 2026 management reports a USD 3 billion programme completed by the second quarter results, a further USD 3 billion programme to run to the end of the second quarter of 2027, 4.8 billion repurchased and 2.8 billion of dividend accrued year to date at Q3, and 1.2 billion more intended over the next three months (Q2 call page:3; Q3 call page:3). Management links the pace to maintaining a CET1 ratio of around 14% and to the Swiss Parliament's deliberations (Q2 call page:3). These are distributions funded from reported earnings and are conditioned on a stated capital ratio. The capital-return plan for 2027 is to be given with fourth quarter results (Q3 call page:3).
### Ownership, governance and behaviour
| Behaviour observed | Category | Evidence | Mechanic and legal-capacity link |

| No sponsor or controlling holder disclosed; only two holders above 3% | Documentary Fact | 20-F page:262: only two holders above 3% | No sponsor-led dividend recapitalisation or fee leakage is evidenced; sponsor alignment is not applicable. Legal capacity under governing documents is not assessed |

| Capital returns within a ratio target | Analyst Interpretation | 20-F page:48 guidance of around 14% CET1; Q3 call page:5 expects year-end ratio "at or very close to our target of around 14%" | Supportive-to-neutral: distributions are tied to a capital buffer and earnings; feasibility is shown by the ratios in the financial base handoff; willingness to reduce buybacks if capital rules tighten is stated by management only |

| Release of the integration capital buffer from 2027 | Management Language | Q3 call page:14: management intends to free up the buffer over minimum requirements from 1 January 2027 | Mixed: it can raise distribution capacity before the Swiss rule outcome is known. Management says earnings capacity allows capital to be built later (page:19). Willingness is stated, outcome not evidenced |

| Opposition to Swiss capital proposals | Management Language | Q1 call page:4 and Q3 call pages:3 and 4: proposals "not proportionate", shareholders called the "first line of defense" | Management positioning. It signals that distributions and structure may be protected against creditor-relevant capital builds; no action on this is evidenced |

| Contingency planning | Insufficient Information | Q3 call pages:10 and 17: management declines to discuss contingency plans | Not an adverse conclusion; the question was asked by analysts and not answered |

| Creditor-adverse actions (priming, uptiering, drop-downs, non-pro-rata exchanges) | Insufficient Information | None found in the sources read; the Q3 liability management action's terms are not supplied | Absence in a limited pack is not evidence of absence. Debt documents are not supplied |

| 1 January 2029 | Capital ordinance affects UBS capital per management | Management Language | Q3 call page:14; future |
### Regulatory and capital-rule context

- The 20-F states that proposed legislation would require deduction of investments in foreign subsidiaries of systemically important banks from CET1 capital, entering into force in 2028 at the earliest, with a 65% deduction in the first year rising by 5-percentage-point steps to 100% (page:88).

- The company states: "We currently estimate that UBS AG would be required to hold additional CET1 capital of around USD 22bn if all capital measures were implemented as proposed by the Swiss Federal Council" and that this would raise UBS Group AG's CET1 ratio to around 18.5% from its target of around 14% (page:89). The Q1 call gives the same order of magnitude, "around 22 billion", on top of 15 billion already required (page:4).

- The 20-F states FINMA's preferred resolution strategy is a single point of entry at UBS Group AG, with write-down of equity, AT1 and tier 2 and conversion of senior unsecured bonds of UBS Group AG to equity if required (page:84). This is a description of the stated strategy, not a legal interpretation of creditor ranking.

- Credit Suisse AT1 litigation: cases lodged against FINMA over the AT1 write-down, with UBS Group AG a party as successor (20-F page:113); management says no decision is expected before the first quarter of 2027 (Q3 call page:14). Provisions are in the financial base handoff; no claim amount is supplied.
### Conflicts and unreconciled items
| Item | Spans | Effect | Resolution as logged |

| Cost-to-achieve figure | Q1 call page:5: "we've incurred costs to achieve of around 13.7 billion at constant FX"; Q1 call page:5: cumulative gross savings of 11.5 billion and a 1.1 times multiple; Q3 call page:5: "total to around 13.7 billion" for gross cost reductions | The same figure appears for costs incurred in one call and for total gross savings in another; the multiple is not defined in the pack, so the two cannot be reconciled | Logged, not reconciled. Do not use either as a cost-to-achieve amount |

| Headcount measures | 20-F page:37: internal and external personnel 119,589 and internal full-time equivalents 103,177; Q3 call page:5: "Total headcount at quarter-end was 110 thousand" | Different bases; the call does not say which base it uses | Logged, not reconciled |
### Credit translations

- Revenue durability. Evidence: net interest income is 7,747 USD m of 49,573 USD m total revenues and Global Wealth Management earns recurring net fee income on fee-generating assets (20-F pages:409 and 49 to 50). Mechanic: revenue depends on market levels, client activity and asset flows more than on loan margins, so revenue moves with markets. Implication: debt service capacity for a group of this size rests on earnings volatility and capital buffers, not on contractual interest cover; the financial base handoff gives the capital and liquidity figures. A logged conflict that counters part of this: none on revenue; the headcount measure conflict only affects cost-per-head analysis.

- Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: operating expenses of 40,197 USD m and a reported cost / income ratio of 81.1% for FY2025, with management targeting below 70% underlying by year-end 2026 (20-F pages:371, 37, 47). Mechanic: integration cost savings are the planned margin driver, but they require integration expenses (Q3 call page:5). Implication: the margin path depends on completing the integration; the target is management language and the cost-to-achieve conflict above limits how far the savings economics can be checked.

- Concentration risk. Evidence: Switzerland provides 32% of revenue and 49% of non-current assets, and the wealth and bank divisions carry most divisional profit (20-F pages:410, 409). Mechanic: Swiss regulation, the Swiss economy and the Swiss capital rules touch both the largest region and the group's legal structure. Implication: a Swiss rule change has outsized effect on distributions and structure; the company's own estimate of around USD 22bn extra CET1 at the bank subsidiary is the size marker.

- Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor or controlling holder disclosed (20-F page:262) and capital returns tied to a ratio target. Mechanic: there is no sponsor incentive for debt-funded extraction, but shareholder distributions compete with capital builds. Implication: monitor distribution decisions against the Swiss rule outcome; no extraction behaviour is evidenced and no conclusion on willingness is drawn.

- Key uncertainties. Swiss capital rules and timing; Credit Suisse AT1 and merger-law litigation; the unverified year-end integration completion; the unknown terms of the Q3 liability management; and ratings in force at the as-of date.

## Calculations

| C3 | Segment profit sums to group | 5,207 + 2,497 + 719 + 2,819 - 1,199 - 1,190 | 8,853 USD m | Matches group operating profit before tax; segment revenues sum to 49,574 against 49,573, rounding |

| C5 | Cumulative gross cost savings path (management, bn) | 10.7 (year-end 2025) + 0.8 = 11.5; 11.5 + 1.1 = 12.6; 12.6 + 0.6 = 13.2; 13.2 + 0.5 = 13.7 | Consistent | 20-F page:41; Q1 call page:5; Q2 call page:4; Q3 call page:4 and page:5 |

| C6 | Repurchases consistency (management, bn) | 3.0 programme completed + 1.8 of the next programme = 4.8 year to date; 4.8 + 1.2 = 6.0 | Consistent with two programmes of 3.0 | Assumes the first programme was executed within 2026; Q2 call page:3 and Q3 call page:3 |

| C8 | Cost-to-achieve check | 11.5 x 1.1 = 12.65 against a stated 13.7 | Does not reconcile | The multiple is not defined in the pack; see conflicts |

spans.text: # CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis: UBS Group AG (ubs)
## Request

UBS Group AG (issuer id `ubs`), as of 2026-11-05 (information cutoff 2026-11-05), pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD. The scope is the fundamental credit view from the reported financial base and the business and transaction context, for a creditor of the group. Prohibited and not done: peer ranking, instrument recommendation and any expected recovery outcome.
## Sources

Issuer sources relied on (pinned `.jsonl` text; locators are `page:N` extraction chunks). The credit view rests on the upstream handoffs below; the issuer sources were opened to check the capital requirements, the Swiss proposals and the funding notes cited in this handoff.
